# S98 - Callback tokens: poll and resume a waiting request (EX10)

26 October 2026. Implements roadmap item EX10 ([docs/25 section 5](../25-studio-and-integration-roadmap.md#5-ex10---resume-and-poll-api-for-waiting-requests)). Shares its callback model with IN05 ([S99](S99-webhooks-and-kafka-triggers.md)). Builds on S16 (message waits), S47/S73 (signed inbound events) and S66/S76 (external-worker callbacks).

## Decisions

| # | Question | Decision |
|---|---|---|
| D1 | New step kind or an option? | **An option on the existing "Wait for a message" step**: `config.externalCallback = { tokenValidFor: <ISO duration> }`. The wait already has the right engine shape (message catch event, optional time limit with a `timedOut` route, declared and type-checked payload fields that become step outputs, buffering, timeline). A new kind would duplicate all of that and add a second way into the engine. Without the option the step, its BPMN and its runtime are byte-for-byte unchanged, so no golden file moves. |
| D2 | Token model | One **callback wait** row per (request, wait step) - created when the request reaches a wait whose step has `externalCallback`. A **token** for it is minted by `POST .../callback-waits/{waitId}/token` (fresh `run.operate`, also allowed to machine clients with that grant), **returned once** in that response and never again. Issuing again replaces the token (the old one stops working at once; audited as revoke + issue). We do not mint a secret at wait start because nobody is there to receive it and the secret must not be stored or queued in clear text anywhere. |
| D3 | Token format and hashing | `ocb_` + 43 characters of base64url (256 random bits from `SecureRandom`). Stored only as **SHA-256 hex** (unique index), never in clear, never logged or audited. A fast hash is correct for 256-bit random secrets (no dictionary to protect); lookups are by hash, so there is no timing oracle on the comparison. |
| D4 | Scope | A token resolves to exactly one wait row, which fixes workspace, request and step. The poll/resume routes carry the workspace in the path and the token in the `X-Orqix-Callback-Token` header (never in a URL or query, so it does not reach access logs). A token presented under another workspace, an unknown, replaced or revoked token, or no token: **404** with the same body as an unknown resource - no oracle. There is no request or step id in the resume call, so a token cannot be pointed at anything else. |
| D5 | Expiry | `tokenValidFor` from the step (PT1M..P30D, compiler-checked). Expiry counts from issue. An expired token can still **poll** (state `expired`) but cannot resume. Expiry is audited once by the sweeper (`callback.token-expired`). The wait itself is unaffected: it still ends by its own time limit or by an operator. |
| D6 | States on poll | `waiting` (token valid, wait open, request active), `resumed` (this token resumed it; carries the original result), `expired`, `cancelled` with a `reason`: `timedOut`, `requestEnded`, `answeredElsewhere` (an ordinary message reached the wait first). A suspended request still reports `waiting` with `suspended: true`. |
| D7 | Cheap polling | `GET` returns a strong ETag `"cbw-<version>-<state>"` built from a row version (bumped on every change) and the computed state; `If-None-Match` with the current tag answers **304** with no body. One indexed lookup by hash, no engine call. `Cache-Control: no-store`. |
| D8 | Resume path | `POST .../callbacks/wait/resume` with `Idempotency-Key` and `{ "result": { ... } }`. The service writes an `inbound_message` row for the step's message name and the wait's own correlation key and hands it to the **existing `MessageDelivery.deliver`** (the same lock order, payload validation against the declared fields, step outputs, `WAIT_ENDED` timeline entry and Flowable `messageEventReceived`). There is no second path into the engine. |
| D9 | One resume per wait | The callback row is locked first. After a successful resume it stores the idempotency key, request hash and the result body. Same key and same body: **200** with the original result and `Idempotent-Replayed: true`. Any other key or body: **409 `CALLBACK_ALREADY_RESUMED`**. A wait that closed another way: **409 `CALLBACK_NOT_WAITING`**. An invalid result (types, unknown or missing required fields, size, depth): **422** and the wait stays open so the caller can correct it. |
| D10 | Relation to operator `resumeRun` | Different things, never conflated. `resumeRun` lifts an operator **suspension** of the whole request (run.operate, reason required). A callback **completes one wait** with a result. A callback against a suspended request is refused with **409 `RUN_SUSPENDED`** and nothing is stored; it can be repeated with the same idempotency key after the operator resumes. API words: "suspend/resume request" stay on the run; the callback API says "resume the wait" and the UI says "Answer from the external system". |
| D11 | Bounds | Result: at most `orqix.messages.max-payload-bytes` (16 KiB default) serialized, depth 10, only the step's declared scalar fields (at most 10). Per workspace at most 10,000 live tokens (issued, unexpired, unresumed); beyond that issuing answers 429 and the waits themselves are unaffected. |
| D12 | Audit | `callback.token-issued` (waitId, runId, nodeId, expiresAt-seconds), `callback.token-revoked` (waitId, runId, replaced), `callback.resumed` (waitId, runId, fieldCount, replayed=false), `callback.token-expired` (waitId, runId). Ids and counts only: never the token, its hash, the correlation key or result values. |
| D12a | Revoking after a resume | Refused with 409 `CALLBACK_ALREADY_RESUMED`: after the resume the token only replays the original answer, and revoking it would turn a safe replay into a 404 (review fix). |
| D13 | Permissions | Issue, revoke and list: `run.operate` (fresh for issue and revoke). Poll and resume: possession of the token only (`x-orqix-permission: callbackToken`), on a separate stateless security chain with CSRF off (no ambient credential), the same pattern as the signed inbound route. No new permission. |
| D14 | Multi-replica | Everything is in PostgreSQL. Resume locks the callback row, then the request, then the subscription (the S16 order). The expiry sweeper uses `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, so any number of pods can run it. |

## What was built

- **Contract** (`contracts/workflow-v0.schema.json`): `waitForMessageNode.config.externalCallback` (`tokenValidFor`, required inside the object). Compiler (`MessageRules`): `WF_CALLBACK_TOKEN_VALIDITY` (outside PT1M..P30D or not a duration). BPMN: the `orqix:message` extension gains `callbackTokenValidFor` **only when the option is set**; `BpmnReader` reads it back so BPMN source editing keeps the option.
- **Migration `V170__callback_waits.sql`**: `callback_wait` (one row per subscription; token hash unique; state columns; result snapshot; version).
- **Runtime**: `CallbackWaits` (created from `MessageWaits.started` inside the engine transaction), `CallbackService` (issue, revoke, list, poll, resume), `CallbackSweeper` (expiry audit), `CallbackController`, security chain `callbackChain` (`@Order(0)`), machine route for issue.
- **API**: `listCallbackWaits`, `issueCallbackToken`, `revokeCallbackToken`, `pollCallbackWait`, `resumeCallbackWait`; problem codes `CALLBACK_ALREADY_RESUMED`, `CALLBACK_NOT_WAITING`.
- **UI**: Studio "Wait for a message" inspector gains "Answered by an external system" with token validity and a read-only contract panel (poll/resume routes, header, declared result fields). Run detail shows an "External system waits" panel to people with `run.operate`: state, expiry, Issue token (shown once, copy with a "Copied" or failure announcement), Revoke. Only the sentence "Token issued. Copy it now" is in a live region; the token itself is never announced by screen readers.

Evidence and exclusions are recorded at the end of [S99](S99-webhooks-and-kafka-triggers.md#evidence), which covers both items.
